name: agent-browser
works_with: Any coding agent that can run shell commands, plus MCP clients
short: A command line browser from Vercel Labs that your AI agent drives one short shell command at a time.
what: agent-browser is a native Rust CLI that gives an AI agent a browser. `snapshot` returns the page as compact text, with a ref such as `@e1` for each element. The agent acts on a ref, reads the page again to check the result, and repeats. The browser stays open between commands, and a background daemon controls it over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
who: People who want their coding agent to open pages, click through flows, fill forms or take screenshots from the shell. If your agent never needs a browser, you can skip it.
needs: Chrome for Testing, which `agent-browser install` downloads the first time

steps.title: Install the CLI
steps.text: With Homebrew, run `brew install agent-browser` and then `agent-browser install`. On Linux, `agent-browser install --with-deps` also installs the browser's system libraries.

steps.title: Try the quick start
steps.text: Refs describe the page at the moment of the snapshot. After a navigation or a page change, take a new snapshot before using refs again.
steps.code:
agent-browser open example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser click @e1
agent-browser get url
agent-browser close

steps.title: Give your agent the skill
steps.text: The installed skill is a small stub that tells the agent to load `agent-browser skills get core`, so its instructions always match the CLI you have installed.

steps.title: Optional: use it over MCP
steps.text: This starts an MCP server over stdio for MCP clients.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `agent-browser open example.com`, then `agent-browser snapshot -i`. You should see `- link "Learn more" [ref=e1]`.

watch: Your agent gets a real browser it can click, type and run `eval` in, so any site it visits is open to it. The Security docs cover an auth vault, domain allowlists and action policies.
A headless browser's daemon keeps running in the background and exits after one hour without commands.
A click fails when the target is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport or covered, for example by a consent banner. Dismiss it, take a new snapshot and retry.
